title: Dexmedetomidine
sources: Probable Dexmedetomidine Induced Diabetes Insipidus: A Case Review. 2021. PMID 34670426
Uddin S, et al. Dexmedetomidine Induced Polyuria in the Intensive Care Unit. Case Reports in Critical Care. 2021. doi:10.1155/2021/8850116
A nephrogenic mechanism underlies dexmedetomidine-induced polyuria: a case report. ScienceDirect, 2023 (three-mechanism model)

changelog.change: Added the polyuria / diabetes-insipidus-mimic caution (3-pathway AVP-AQP2 mechanism, recognition, and management) from the CV Dexmedetomidine & Polyuria guide.
Imported from AnesCalc v2 DrugCard.swift via tools/import-anescalc.mjs.

mechanism: Selective α₂-adrenergic agonist → inhibits NE release from locus coeruleus (sedation/anxiolysis) and dorsal horn (analgesia/sympatholysis). Produces cooperative, rousable sedation without respiratory depression.
dosing:
Loading: 1 mcg/kg over 10 min (omit if hemodynamically unstable)
Maintenance: 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr (titrate to RASS/BIS)
Procedural/awake intubation: 0.5–1 mcg/kg over 10 min load; 0.2–0.5 mcg/kg/hr maintenance
cautions: AEs: Bradycardia (including sinus arrest), hypotension, transient hypertension (rapid bolus), dry mouth, nausea
CI: No absolute contraindications per FDA
Precautions: Avoid in 2nd/3rd degree AV block, uncompensated heart failure; continuous monitoring required; tolerance/tachyphylaxis with prolonged infusion; NOT interchangeable with clonidine

Polyuria / DI mimic: can cause a lot of dilute urine (>3 mL/kg/hr, osmolality <250-300 mOsm/kg) via a 3-pathway hit on the AVP-AQP2 axis (central AVP suppression, direct renal AQP2 effect, imidazoline-receptor salt/water loss). Reported after a single loading dose and at rates as low as 0.2 mcg/kg/hr — not just high-dose/prolonged infusions. The tell is timing: starts with the infusion, resolves within hours of stopping it. Untreated, sodium climbs while potassium can fall sharply — the electrolyte shift, not the urine volume, is what kills (a published case: Na 156, K < 1.8, Torsades). Confirm with UOP/Na/osmolality/glucose, rule out osmotic diuresis, diuretics, true central/nephrogenic DI, and post-obstructive diuresis, then stop or reduce the infusion and replace electrolytes gently — DDAVP is rarely needed.
pearls: Produces cooperative sedation — patient rousable and NOT apneic. Ideal for awake fiber-optic intubation or procedures requiring patient cooperation.
Synergistic with opioids for analgesia. Load dose ARDS/resp failure with infusions >24h — associated with outcomes concerns in some ICU data.
